article.title: NFL EDGE Thursday Evening Brief
article.dek: The Bears stole one in Detroit at the gun, Dallas is rolling Philadelphia late, and the board swapped two of its three Sunday cards.

items.headline: Bears 39, Lions 35 — Williams wins it with three seconds left
paragraphs: The Bears stole the Thanksgiving opener in Detroit. Caleb Williams hit Rome Odunze for a 6-yard touchdown with three seconds left, finishing a 13-play, 68-yard drive. It was Chicago's first lead of the game.
Jahmyr Gibbs ran for 205 yards and three touchdowns in the loss, and Jared Goff threw for 313 yards. It was not enough. The Bears are 9-2 now, alone on top of the NFC North. The Lions fall to 8-3.
The model liked Detroit by more than the market did. That lean did not survive the final drive.
items.takeaway: Detroit led most of the day and lost it at the gun. Nothing to bet after the fact — the board's Sunday cards are where the action is now.

items.headline: Cowboys 38, Eagles 30 late — Dallas is rolling, Philly keeps answering
paragraphs: This one was still going when the brief was written, with Dallas up 38-30 and 7:30 left in the fourth quarter. Dallas led 28-10 at halftime and has controlled it since.

Dak Prescott has thrown for 258 yards and two touchdowns and run for another. Javonte Williams has three total touchdowns. Joe Milton, starting for Philadelphia with Jalen Hurts out, threw his first touchdown pass as an Eagle — a 50-yard strike to DeVonta Smith.
The final score lands in the morning brief. Do not bet the middle of a game that is already nearly decided.
items.takeaway: Dallas has owned this one since the first half. The result was not final when this was written — check the morning brief for the final.

items.headline: Thursday injury board: Watson is in protocol, Johnson starts again in Buffalo
paragraphs: Christian Watson is in the concussion protocol after the hit from Rams safety Kamren Kinchens on Wednesday night. The concussion was confirmed after Watson was evaluated in the locker room. He is uncertain for Week 13, and Green Bay does not play again until Sunday, Dec. 6, against New Orleans.

The night game's inactives are set. Kenneth Walker III is out for a third straight game, so rookie Emmett Johnson starts again for Kansas City after back-to-back 100-yard games. Jaylon Moore and Omarr Norman-Lott are out too. Patrick Mahomes, Rashee Rice and Trey Smith carry no designation. For Buffalo, Dalton Kincaid and Christian Benford are questionable.
items.takeaway: The night game's backfield is settled — Johnson again. Watson is a next-week question, not a tonight question.

items.headline: Rain and wind tonight in Buffalo; showers Friday in Pittsburgh
paragraphs: The night game kicks off at 8:20 p.m. ET in the rain. Buffalo is looking at rain all night, mid-30s, wind around 19 mph with gusts near 30. A gale warning runs until 1:00 a.m. Friday.
Tomorrow is wet too. Denver at Pittsburgh kicks off at 3:00 p.m. ET on Friday at Acrisure Stadium, with showers, a high of 41, a 70% chance of rain and wind around 15 mph.
items.takeaway: Two wet, windy outdoor games in a row. Weather is a fact to know, not a totals edge on its own.

sections.title: What It Means for NFL EDGE

items.headline: The board swapped two of its three cards
paragraphs: Hit Rate is now San Francisco moneyline -146. The model gives the 49ers a 73.7% chance to win. That is the job of Hit Rate: which supported pick looks most likely to win. It is not the plus-expected-value play, and it is not supposed to be. Hit Rate is not Profit Rate.

Balanced stays New England moneyline, now -120 after sitting at -116 this morning. The model gives the Patriots a 58.3% chance. Value is now Indianapolis +6.5 at -115, the model's plus-expected-value play — but the edge is thin, +0.7%, after this morning's Chargers card carried +4.5%.
When the board swaps a card, the old card is off. Cleveland moneyline and Chargers +1.5 are not bets anymore. Check the board as it stands now.
items.takeaway: Two new cards, one same pick at a worse price. The board as it stands now is the only board that counts.

items.headline: No card on tonight or tomorrow — use Check
paragraphs: All three cards are Sunday games. The board has no card on Chiefs-Bills tonight or Broncos-Steelers tomorrow.

The model is cooler than the market on both favorites. It has Buffalo by 0.7 against a market of Buffalo -3, and Denver by 1.8 against a market of Denver -4.5. If your book has a number you like on either game, tap Check, type in the line and price, and the app runs it back through the model and evaluator for a bet or no-bet verdict on your price.
items.takeaway: No card is not a no. It means the board is quiet — Check your own number.

items.headline: Steam: when a line moves in a hurry
paragraphs: Steam is a line that moves fast — usually within minutes — when a lot of money hits one side at once. The number jumps because money moved it, not because the football changed.
Here is a clearly labeled hypothetical. Say a team opens at -3 on Sunday morning and by lunch it is -5, with no injury news at all. That is steam. The early number is gone.
Chasing a steamed number means paying the worst of it. If you liked the team at -3, the moment has passed. Wait for the number to come back, or check whether the other side now has value at +5.
items.takeaway: Steam tells you money moved, not that the football changed — never chase a steamed number, check whether the other side is the value now.

items.headline: Two cards replaced, one card repriced
paragraphs: Morning to evening, the board moved. Hit Rate went from Cleveland moneyline -230 to San Francisco moneyline -146. Value went from Chargers +1.5 at -115 to Indianapolis +6.5 at -115.

Balanced is the same pick, repriced: New England moneyline -116 this morning, -120 now on FanDuel, with the play-through moving from -119 to -123. The Cleveland and Chargers cards are gone from the board.
items.takeaway: The board moved while the day went on. Bet the card as it stands, not the one from this morning.

items.headline: New England's spread moved a point on DraftKings
paragraphs: The Patriots were -1.5 on DraftKings this morning. They are -2.5 now. FanDuel still has New England -1.5, so the same game carries a different number depending on your book.
Denver -4.5 and Buffalo -3 are unchanged since the morning, and the Buffalo total is still 45.5. Cleveland's moneyline is -244 on DraftKings and -225 on FanDuel, against -230 on FanDuel this morning.
items.takeaway: New England moved a point on DraftKings while FanDuel held at -1.5 — same game, different number by book. That is what Check is for.

items.headline: Friday is a Check day — and the Sunday cards are already moving
paragraphs: Broncos-Steelers kicks off Friday at 3:00 p.m. ET in Pittsburgh, and the board has no card on it. If your book has a number you like, run it through Check before kickoff.

One timing note: the Balanced card got more expensive while the day went on, -116 to -120. A good number now beats a hoped-for number Sunday — waiting lets the number drift the wrong way too. And do not bet Thursday's results into Friday.
items.takeaway: Check your Friday number before kickoff, and if a Sunday card has a good number now, take it now.

evidence.fact: Chicago beat Detroit 39-35 on Thursday, Nov 26, 2026, at Ford Field. Caleb Williams threw a 6-yard touchdown pass to Rome Odunze with 3 seconds left, capping a 13-play, 68-yard drive. The Bears trailed for nearly the whole game and took their first lead on the final play. Jahmyr Gibbs ran 21 times for 205 yards and three touchdowns for Detroit. Jared Goff completed 25 of 36 passes for 313 yards and one touchdown with one interception. Williams threw for 345 yards. Chicago improved to 9-2 and took first place in the NFC North; Detroit fell to 8-3.
evidence.interpretation: Detroit led most of the day and lost it at the gun. The model liked Detroit by more than the market did, and that lean did not survive the final drive.

evidence.fact: Dallas leads Philadelphia 38-30 in the fourth quarter (7:30 left) on Thursday, Nov 26, 2026, at AT&T Stadium, in a game still in progress at brief time. Dallas led 28-10 at halftime. Dak Prescott has thrown for 258 yards and two touchdowns and run for another; Javonte Williams has three total touchdowns (two rushing, one receiving). Joe Milton, starting at quarterback for Philadelphia with Jalen Hurts out, threw his first touchdown pass as an Eagle, a 50-yard strike to DeVonta Smith.
evidence.interpretation: Dallas has controlled the game since the first half, but Philadelphia has kept answering in the second half. The result is not final at brief time.

evidence.fact: Green Bay WR Christian Watson is in the concussion protocol after the hit from Rams safety Kamren Kinchens late in the first half of Wednesday night's game against the Rams. Watson had four catches for 65 yards and a touchdown before leaving, and the concussion was confirmed after he was evaluated in the locker room. Kinchens was ejected for the helmet-to-helmet hit. Watson is uncertain for Week 13; Green Bay does not play again until Sunday, Dec 6, against New Orleans, so he has extra time to clear protocol.
evidence.interpretation: Watson was Green Bay's leading receiver going into Wednesday night. His Week 13 status is a watch item for next week, not this one.

evidence.fact: Final inactives for Kansas City at Buffalo, Thursday Nov 26, 2026, 8:20 p.m. ET kickoff: Chiefs RB Kenneth Walker III (groin) is OUT for a third straight game; rookie Emmett Johnson starts for a third straight game after back-to-back 100-yard rushing games. Kansas City also ruled out OT Jaylon Moore (ankle) and DT Omarr Norman-Lott (knee); TE Noah Gray (rib) and DL Peter Woods (neck) are questionable. QB Patrick Mahomes (knee, right elbow), WR Rashee Rice (knee), G Trey Smith (concussion) and CB Mansoor Delane (shoulder) carry no designation and are set to play. Buffalo listed TE Dalton Kincaid (thumb, ankle) and CB Christian Benford (groin) as questionable.
evidence.interpretation: Kansas City's backfield is settled: Johnson again. Buffalo's two questionable starters are the last open question before kickoff.

evidence.fact: Kansas City at Buffalo, Thursday Nov 26, 2026, 8:20 p.m. ET kickoff at Highmark Stadium (open air): rain through the afternoon and night, 100% chance at kickoff, around 35 to 36 degrees, wind east-northeast around 18 to 19 mph with gusts near 30 mph. A gale warning runs 2:00 p.m. Thursday to 1:00 a.m. Friday.
evidence.interpretation: A wet, windy night in Buffalo for the night game.

evidence.fact: Denver at Pittsburgh, Friday Nov 27, 2026, 3:00 p.m. ET kickoff at Acrisure Stadium (open air): showers expected, high 41 degrees, rain chance 70%, wind southwest around 15 mph. Overnight rain is expected Thursday into Friday, with rain or snow possible late Friday night.
evidence.interpretation: A wet, cold, windy afternoon in Pittsburgh. Weather is a fact to know, not a totals edge on its own.
